title: Sorting, Map and Set
summary: The default string sort trap, comparators, toSorted, and the Map and Set collections.

steps.title: The sort trap
body: `sort()` without arguments converts every element to a **string** and sorts those:
Always pass a **comparator**: negative means `a` first, positive means `b` first (like C# `Comparison<T>`):
`sort` also **mutates** the array in place and returns it. In code that must not mutate (React state!), use `toSorted`, which returns a sorted copy:
const sorted = scores.toSorted((a, b) => b - a);   // descending, scores untouched

code: const b = a.toSorted((x, y) => x - y);
steps.explain: Without a comparator the numbers sort as strings: `"1" < "100" < "25" < "5"`. `toSorted` with `x - y` sorts numerically and leaves `a` alone.

steps.prompt: Which call sorts `products` by `price` from highest to lowest without changing `products`?
steps.explain: `toSorted` copies; `b - a` puts larger prices first. `sort` would mutate.

steps.title: Map and Set
body: A plain object works as a string-keyed dictionary, but `Map` is the real `Dictionary<K, V>`: any key type, insertion order kept, and a `size`.
for (const [k, v] of stock) console.log(k, v);
Keys compare like `===`, so two different objects with the same contents are two different keys. Note that `JSON.stringify(new Map(...))` gives `{}`: convert with `Object.fromEntries(map)` first.

steps.explain: A set keeps the first occurrence of each value, in insertion order. `!` is a TypeScript-only "not undefined" assertion that Node simply strips.

steps.title: Word frequency
prompt: Write `wordCounts(text)` that counts words using a `Map<string, number>` and returns the result as an array of `[word, count]` pairs, most frequent first, ties alphabetical.
Words are lower-cased and split on spaces; ignore empty strings.
template: Dojo.eq('wordCounts("the cat and The hat")', [["the", 2], ["and", 1], ["cat", 1], ["hat", 1]], wordCounts("the cat and The hat"));
Dojo.eq("extra spaces ignored", [["b", 2], ["a", 1]], wordCounts("b  a b "));
hints: `[...counts]` turns the map into `[key, value]` pairs you can sort.
